construct.diagnosis_or_process: Hypomagnesemia with secondary hypocalcemia due to TRPM6 dysfunction
construct.mechanism: TRPM6 channels mediate magnesium absorption in intestine and magnesium reabsorption in the distal convoluted tubule. Loss of function causes profound hypomagnesemia; severe magnesium deficiency suppresses PTH secretion and impairs PTH action, producing secondary hypocalcemia and neuromuscular irritability.
construct.primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

second_answer_attack.resolution: Gitelman can cause hypomagnesemia, but it is an NCC salt-wasting disorder usually accompanied by hypokalemic alkalosis and hypocalciuria. Profound infantile hypomagnesemia, secondary hypocalcemia with low-normal PTH, failure of calcium-only therapy, and biallelic TRPM6 identify the primary magnesium-transport defect.
